title: Sequential limits along epimorphisms on a weakly contractible object
statement:
Let $(F_n,t_n)$ be an inverse sequence of sheaves of sets on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with
epimorphic transition maps, and let $W$ be a weakly contractible object. Then every
$t_n(W)\colon F_{n+1}(W)\to F_n(W)$ is surjective, and for every $m$ the projection
$(\varprojlim_nF_n)(W)\to F_m(W)$ is surjective.

proof.text: For every $n\geq0$, apply condition 3 of [det-pe-weak-contractible-equivalences] to the epimorphism $t_n:F_{n+1}\to F_n$ and the given weakly contractible object $W$. It gives that $t_n(W):F_{n+1}(W)\to F_n(W)$ is surjective, proving the first assertion.

source.place: First sentence: surjectivity of t_n(W) is part 3 of the weak-contractibility equivalences

proof.text: Fix $m\geq0$ and a prescribed $a\in F_m(W)$. For each $n$ and $z\in F_n(W)$, use classical choice on the nonempty fibre of $t_n(W)$ over $z$ to choose $s_n(z)\in F_{n+1}(W)$ with $t_n(W)(s_n(z))=z$. Define $b_0=a$ and $b_{r+1}=s_{m+r}(b_r)$ by recursion on $r\in\mathbf N$. Inductively $b_r\in F_{m+r}(W)$, and the displayed choice equation gives $t_{m+r}(W)(b_{r+1})=b_r$ for every $r$. Thus all stages from $m$ upwards have compatible chosen values. This is only set-theoretic choice and natural-number recursion; no sheaf morphisms $s_n$ or choices compatible with restrictions are asserted.

source.place: Middle sentence: successive lifts above m, with the dependent-choice construction expanded as chosen preimages and recursion

proof.text: Set $x_{m+r}=b_r$ for $r\geq0$, and define the finitely many earlier values by $x_n=t_n(W)(x_{n+1})$ in descending order for $n=m-1,\ldots,0$. For $n<m$ the identity $t_n(W)(x_{n+1})=x_n$ holds by this definition; for $n=m+r\geq m$ it is the identity proved in step 2. Hence $(x_n)$ is compatible at every adjacent pair and $x_m=b_0=a$. If $m=0$, there are no earlier values to define.

source.place: Middle sentence: earlier stages determined by descending transition maps; verify compatibility in both index ranges

proof.text: The formula in [det-pe-replete-definition] identifies $(\varprojlim_n F_n)(W)$ with the tuples $(x_n)\in\prod_n F_n(W)$ satisfying $t_n(W)(x_{n+1})=x_n$ for all $n$, and identifies its $m$-th projection with $(x_n)\mapsto x_m$. The tuple constructed in steps 2 and 3 therefore defines an element of this section set whose $m$-th projection is the prescribed $a$. Since $a$ and $m$ were arbitrary, every displayed projection is surjective.

source.place: Final sentence: sectionwise inverse-limit description and its coordinate projection

proof_origin.place: Entire proof, expanded into transition surjectivity, explicit recursive lifts, finite backward extension, and the sectionwise limit formula
